brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.

requirements.evidence: Two adjacent cells at 0,0,0 and 1,0,0 each fitted with hex-bin-full (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full). Open faces capped and joints locked. Fork and knife props placed on bench to indicate utensil use; bins available as holders.

The configurator checks geometry and fit only, not sealing, layer adhesion, or water resistance. Parts are 3D-printed in user-chosen material; waterproofness depends on material, print settings and post-processing which cannot be verified here. Shape provides open bins but no guarantee of water-tightness.

The configurator checks fit and collisions only. It has no data on heat resistance, food safety, or dishwasher compatibility. Parts are 3D-printed plastic in a material the user chooses; dishwasher safety cannot be claimed from geometry alone. No material or process to meet this is visible.

finish.summary: Built compact two-cell base with a full-depth bin in each cell as utensil holder. Dressed with fork/knife on bench to show purpose. Waterproof and dishwasher-safe cannot be met by geometry alone – they are material/process claims the system does not verify.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
